title: Governance beyond borders: exploring executive overconfidence and firm performance using meta-analysis

summary.oneLiner: Pooling 116 effect sizes worldwide, this meta-analysis finds that country-level governance factors significantly shape how executive overconfidence relates to firm performance.
summary.overview: Studies disagree on whether overconfident executives help or hurt their firms. This paper pools results from many prior studies (a meta-analysis) across countries to see whether national context explains the inconsistency. The authors test whether differences in governance quality, board effectiveness and shareholder protection change the overconfidence-performance link. They report that country-level factors significantly shape the relationship, and argue that executive traits should be studied together with the institutional setting in which executives operate.
summary.question: Do country-level factors such as governance, board effectiveness and shareholder protection moderate the relationship between executive overconfidence and firm performance?
summary.method: A cross-national meta-analysis, statistically combining effect sizes from prior studies and testing country-level moderators.
summary.data: 116 independent effect sizes from studies around the world. The number of primary studies, countries and years covered are not stated in the available sources.
findings: The relationship between executive overconfidence and firm performance is reported to be significantly shaped by country-level factors.
Governance quality, board effectiveness and shareholder protection are the national-level moderators examined.
The authors argue that contextual influences should be considered alongside trait-based explanations of executive behaviour.
The direction and size of the overall effect are not stated in the available sources.
summary.whyItMatters: The authors advise organisations to build national context into their governance structures when managing the risks of overconfident leaders. For students heading into strategy or board-facing roles, it is a reminder that the same CEO personality may play out differently under different governance regimes.
industries: Not stated in the available sources.
